report.summary: Chunk 8 of 25: defines _head_sha (private) and _repo_state_freshness (private) and inventory_freshness (public). Claims checked: prefix comparison, fail-open, abbreviation validation, single-direction check.
risks: _head_sha | medium | The function is private and may not be tested directly; its logic for resolving HEAD from git dirs is complex and may fail on edge cases (e.g., detached HEAD, packed-refs). | Review test coverage for _head_sha.

_repo_state_freshness | low | The function returns fresh=True when git cannot answer; this could mask actual staleness if git is available but broken. | Verify that failing open is the correct policy for the caller.

_repo_state_freshness | low | The prefix comparison only checks recorded.startswith(actual) but the docstring says actual.startswith(recorded). The code implements actual.startswith(recorded), which is correct for abbreviation. | Confirm the docstring phrasing matches the code.

handoff.purpose: Implements HEAD resolution and freshness checking for repo state stamps.

symbols.name: _head_sha
symbols.note: Private function that resolves HEAD SHA from a git repository. Uses .git file, HEAD ref, loose refs, and packed-refs.

symbols.name: _repo_state_freshness
symbols.note: Private function that compares a recorded repo_state.head against actual HEAD. Returns dict with fresh, reason, recorded_head, actual_head, dirty.

symbols.name: inventory_freshness
symbols.note: Public function that checks freshness of an inventory document by delegating to _repo_state_freshness.

claims.text: The comparison is by PREFIX, because these files record a short sha and git reports a long one
claims.why: Code uses actual.startswith(recorded) which is prefix comparison.

claims.text: A dirty: true snapshot is NOT treated as stale on its own
claims.why: The function returns dirty as a separate field and does not alter freshness based on it.

claims.text: Fails OPEN (fresh: True) when git cannot answer at all
claims.why: When _head_sha returns None, the function returns fresh: True.

claims.text: Without this, a recorded 'a' matches roughly one HEAD in sixteen and the gate silently reports fresh
claims.why: The code validates recorded against _ABBREV_SHA_RE, which requires at least _MIN_ABBREV hex characters (presumably >1).

claims.text: ONE direction only: the file records an abbreviation of the full sha git stores, so actual.startswith(recorded) is the containment that can be true. Testing the reverse as well would let a SHORTER actual satisfy a longer recorded value
claims.why: Code uses actual.startswith(recorded) only, not recorded.startswith(actual).

observations.what: _head_sha is private and not exported; it is used only within _repo_state_freshness.
The docstring for _repo_state_freshness says 'comparison is by PREFIX' and 'actual.startswith(recorded)' but the code does exactly that.
The function _head_sha reads 'commondir' to support linked worktrees, but does not handle the case where commondir file contains a relative path with '..' or symlinks.
The function _head_sha returns None when HEAD is not a valid ref and not a SHA, but does not raise an exception; _repo_state_freshness treats this as 'git could not report HEAD'.
